/-!
# Erdős Problem 591

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/591](https://www.erdosproblems.com/591)
- [Sc10] Schipperus, Rene, Countable partition ordinals. Ann. Pure Appl. Logic (2010), 1195-1215.
-/

open Cardinal Ordinal

namespace Erdos591

universe u

/--
Let $α$ be the infinite ordinal $\omega^{\omega^2}$. Is it true that any red/blue colouring of the
edges of $K_α$ there is either a red $K_α$ or a blue $K_3$?

This is true and was proved independently by Schipperus [Sc10] and Darby.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3]
theorem erdos_591 : answer(True) ↔ OrdinalCardinalRamsey (ω ^ ω ^ 2) (ω ^ ω ^ 2) 3 := by
  sorry

end Erdos591

reformulations.difference: The partition relation is encoded using complementary simple graphs on an ordinal representative, with an order-type condition for the red clique and a cardinality condition for the blue clique, rather than an explicit edge-colouring function.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: IsCompl red blue is equivalent to blue = redᶜ, so the graphs partition all unordered pairs of distinct vertices into exactly two colours. α.ToType has order type α, and typeLT s = α is equivalent to the existence of an order isomorphism s ≃o α.ToType. The condition #s = 3 gives exactly three distinct vertices and, for this inherited well-order, is equivalent to typeLT s = 3. Lean’s inner natural-number power ω ^ 2 agrees with ordinal exponentiation at the finite ordinal 2, so the displayed expression is exactly ω^(ω²). In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, problem_rhs_iff_source proves the full equivalence to arbitrary symmetric Bool colourings, a red order-isomorphic copy, or a blue three-element clique. Its axioms contain no sorryAx.
